text:
The fastest way to kill a Platform Engineering initiative:

Spend 6 months building an Internal Developer Portal that developers didn't ask for.

Automate their top 3 Slack support tickets instead (preview DBs, secrets, DNS).

What was your team's #1 platform win? #PlatformEngineering

90% of enterprise Azure migrations stall for the exact same reason:

It’s never Kubernetes.
It’s never the database.
It’s subscription governance on Day 1.

Automate landing zone guardrails in Terraform before writing a single service. #Azure

The biggest pitfall in enterprise RAG isn't the vector DB or embedding model.

It's chunk boundary quality and metadata filtering.

Without document hierarchy and access scopes, your LLM retrieves garbage with high confidence.

How do you handle chunk overlaps? #AppliedAI

Under Australia's Privacy Act APP 1.7–1.9, companies automating decisions affecting individuals must evidence how decisions were made.

Static PDF policies won't protect you in an OAIC audit.

You need code-layer flight recorders.

Is your AI audit-ready? #RegTech

In enterprise consulting, the hardest problem is rarely technical architecture—it's organizational alignment.

A simple architecture with 100% buy-in beats a 'flawless' system that teams resist using every single time.

Culture eats architecture for breakfast. #TechLead

Managing IT for community non-profits teaches you that security hygiene matters most where budgets are tightest.

Enforcing strict Entra ID MFA and domain security protects vulnerable helplines from compromise with zero extra software cost. #Leadership

Early in your career, you measure progress by how much code you write.

Later on, you measure progress by how much complexity you prevented from reaching production.

What was the turning point for you? #Engineering

Clean Terraform pattern for Azure:

Separate state by lifecycle frequency, not by environment.

VNet / Landing zones (yearly) ≠ AKS clusters (monthly) ≠ App deploys (daily).

Your blast radius immediately shrinks to near zero. Bicep or Terraform in 2026? #DevOps

Developer velocity isn't how fast developers type code.

It's how little friction stands between `git push` and production verification with zero fear of breaking the build.

If you have a 3-week QA sign-off phase, you don't have CI/CD. #Cloud

Building AI agents that work in production requires treating tool calling like distributed systems RPC:

1. Client idempotency keys
2. Strict Zod/Pydantic validation
3. Deterministic fallbacks when models hallucinate args.

Never trust raw LLM JSON. #Architecture

When architecting ADM Guard, rule #1 was zero-PII by design.

If an API payload contains names, emails, or tax IDs, our gateway boundary rejects it with HTTP 422 before persistence.

You cannot leak data you never store. #RegTech #BuildInPublic

After 8+ years shipping enterprise production systems, here is my golden rule:

Design for the failure mode first.

If you don't know what happens when downstream returns HTTP 504 or network partitions, you haven't finished designing. #SoftwareEngineering

The highest-leverage IT work in the non-profit sector isn't migrating to fancy new SaaS tools.

It's deprecating legacy shadow IT, locking down phishing vectors, and giving volunteer case workers tools that never crash. #Leadership

Balancing enterprise consulting while building a tech startup:

The key is zero context-switching during focus blocks.

Enterprise delivery builds discipline; startups demand speed. Both make you a significantly sharper engineer. #BuildingInPublic
